marking_schemes.question_text:
Unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo:
(a) Addition reaction
(b) Substitution reaction
(c) Oxidation reaction
(d) Redox reaction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates answered correctly. A few were confused with Substitution or Oxidation reaction.

marking_schemes.question_text:
In the 2nd period Neon has maximum Ionization Potential because:
(a) It has unstable electronic configuration.
(b) It easily accepts electrons.
(c) It easily loses electrons.
(d) The outer most shell is completely filled.
options: (d) The outer most shell is completely filled.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: (d) The outer most shell is completely filled.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (d) / D / The outer most shell is completely filled.
marking_schemes.model_answer: (d) The outer most shell is completely filled.
accepted_alternatives: The outer most shell is completely filled
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few chose option (a) incorrectly.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
Copper, Zinc and Tin are the metals alloyed to form:
(a) Duralumin
(b) Brass
(c) Bronze
(d) Solder
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority chose Bronze correctly. Some confused Bronze with Brass or Duralumin. Note: Marking scheme accepts both Bronze and Brass.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The metal hydroxide which reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salt and water is:
(a) Calcium hydroxide
(b) Magnesium hydroxide
(c) Aluminium hydroxide
(d) Ferric hydroxide
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) / C / Aluminium hydroxide / Al(OH)3 / Aluminium / Al
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates identified Aluminium hydroxide correctly. A few chose Calcium or Magnesium hydroxide.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 is termed as:
(a) Halogenation
(b) Esterification
(c) Hydrogenation
(d) Dehydrohalogenation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates chose Dehydrohalogenation instead of Esterification.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Conversion of Ethanol to Ethene by the action of concentrated sulphuric acid involves:
(a) Dehydration
(b) Dehydrogenation
(c) Dehydrohalogenation
(d) Hydrolysis
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates chose Dehydrogenation instead of Dehydration. Confusion between dehydrogenation and dehydrohalogenation was common.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The oxidizing agent in the equation S + 2H2SO4 → 3SO2 + 2H2O is:
(a) Sulphur
(b) Sulphuric acid
(c) Sulphur dioxide
(d) Water
key_points: Sulphuric acid is the oxidizing agent
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly. Many confused oxidation concepts and chose Sulphur dioxide.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Electron Affinity is maximum in:
(a) Mg
(b) Ar
(c) Li
(d) Br
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (d) / D / Br / bromine / Br2 / br2 / br
key_points: Bromine has maximum electron affinity among the given options
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority chose Ar or Li instead of Br.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
The compound that is not a constituent of the electrolytic mixture used in the Hall-Heroult's process is:
(a) Al2O3
(b) NaAlO2
(c) Na3AlF6
(d) CaF2
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) / B / NaAlO2 / sodium aluminate / sodium meta aluminate
key_points: NaAlO2 is not a constituent of the Hall-Heroult electrolytic mixture
common_errors: Overlooking the word 'not' in the question
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered NaAlO2 correctly. Some chose Al2O3 or Na3AlF6. Some overlooked the word 'not'.

marking_schemes.question_text:
On passing ammonia gas over heated copper oxide for some time, a reddish-brown residue is left behind. What property of ammonia is demonstrated here?
(a) Basic property
(b) Oxidising property
(c) Reducing property
(d) Acidic property
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) / C / Reducing property / Reducing agent / Reducing
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many were unsure whether ammonia is a reducing or oxidizing agent. Several incorrectly identified it as basic or oxidising.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Rotten egg smell is due to the liberation of:
(a) HCl gas
(b) H2S gas
(c) Cl2 gas
(d) SO2 gas
key_points: H2S gas causes rotten egg smell
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few chose SO2 or HCl.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Ammonia gas is collected by downward displacement of air since ammonia is:
(a) very slightly soluble in water.
(b) heavier than air.
(c) lighter than air.
(d) insoluble in water.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly. A few confused ammonia collection with HCl collection.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Which of the following would occupy 22.4 litres at S.T.P.?
1. 32g of oxygen gas
2. 2 moles of hydrogen gas
3. 6.022 x 10^23 molecules of ammonia
(a) 1 & 2
(b) 1 & 3
(c) 2 & 3
(d) 1, 2 & 3
[Atomic weights: O = 16, H = 1, N = 14]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) / B / 1 & 3 / or 32 gm of oxygen gas and 6.022 x 10^23 molecules of ammonia
key_points: 32g of O2 = 1 mole occupies 22.4 L at STP
6.022x10^23 molecules of NH3 = 1 mole occupies 22.4 L at STP
2 moles of H2 occupies 44.8 L not 22.4 L
accepted_alternatives: 32 gm of oxygen gas and 6.022 x 10^23 molecules of ammonia
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were confused. Several chose options without working out calculations.

marking_schemes.question_text:
In the molecule of water, oxygen atom has:
(a) One shared pair of electrons.
(b) Three shared pairs of electrons.
(c) Two lone pairs of electrons.
(d) One lone pair of electrons.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) / C / Two lone pairs of electrons / 2
key_points: Oxygen in water has two lone pairs of electrons
common_errors: Confusing ammonia lone pairs with water
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many chose one lone pair instead of two. Some confused ammonia and water structures.

marking_schemes.question_text:
A mineral from which the metal can be extracted economically and conveniently is known as:
(a) Matrix
(b) Ore
(c) Flux
(d) Alloy
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly. A few confused with alloy or matrix.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. During electroplating the iron cup is placed at the cathode. Why?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The metal gets deposited / The metal ion gets discharged at the cathode / nickel ions or cations move to the cathode / Ni+2 gets discharged / reduction takes place at the cathode / cathode acts as reducing electrode.
key_points: Metal/nickel ions get discharged/deposited at cathode
marking_schemes.model_answer: The iron cup is placed at the cathode because nickel ions (Ni²⁺) from the electrolyte are attracted to the cathode and get discharged/deposited there. Reduction takes place at the cathode, which acts as the reducing electrode.
accepted_alternatives: The metal gets deposited at cathode
common_errors: Stating 'object to be plated is placed at cathode' without reason
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most failed to give the actual reason. Many used incorrect terms like 'oxidizing electrode' instead of 'reducing electrode'.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. Name the ion that must be present in the electrolyte.
common_errors: Writing Fe (iron) as the ion present
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered Ni²⁺ correctly. Some wrote iron or incorrect valency.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. State one condition that is necessary to ensure that the deposit is smooth, firm and even.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Small / low current for a long period of time / DC should be used / AC should not be used / high current for short period of time should not be used / article should be thoroughly cleaned / article should be dipped completely in the electrolyte
key_points: Low/small current for a long period
marking_schemes.model_answer: A small/low current should be used for a long period of time to ensure the deposit is smooth, firm and even.
accepted_alternatives: Article should be completely dipped in electrolyte
common_errors: Writing 'slow current for a long time' without specifying DC
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most wrote conditions correctly. A few mentioned high current which is incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. Write the reaction taking place at the cathode.
common_errors: Writing equation in reverse: Ni → Ni²⁺
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many got the equation wrong due to confusion with valency of Ni. Some wrote reverse equation.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. What change would you observe at the anode?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The anode decreases in mass / size / becomes thinner / diminishes / reduces / dissolves / used up
marking_schemes.model_answer: The anode (nickel) decreases in mass/size as it dissolves into the electrolyte.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly stated anode diminishes. A few wrote 'no change'.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match the Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) Water, (b) Alkali metal, (c) Halogen, (d) Calcium oxide, (e) Weak acid
Column B: 1. Lithium, 2. Iodine, 3. Covalent compound, 4. Acetic acid, 5. Ionic compound, 6. Sulphuric acid
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Water - 3. Covalent compound; (b) Alkali metal - 1. Lithium; (c) Halogen - 2. Iodine; (d) Calcium oxide - 5. Ionic compound; (e) Weak acid - 4. Acetic acid
key_points: Calcium oxide is an ionic compound
Acetic acid is a weak acid
common_errors: Identifying sulphuric acid as weak acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly. Some confused water and calcium oxide classifications. Some identified sulphuric acid as weak acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct answer from the brackets: The salt that can be prepared by Direct Combination is ___________. [FeCl3 / FeCl2]
key_points: FeCl3 is prepared by direct combination of iron and chlorine
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many incorrectly wrote FeCl2. Confusion between ferrous and ferric chloride.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct answer from the brackets: The metallic oxide which can be reduced by using common reducing agents is __________. [Fe2O3 / Al2O3]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Fe2O3 / ferric oxide / Iron(III) oxide / Fe / Iron
key_points: Fe2O3 can be reduced by common reducing agents; Al2O3 cannot
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many chose Al2O3 incorrectly. Confusion between Fe2O3 and Al2O3 reducibility.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct answer from the brackets: The metal nitrate which on thermal decomposition forms a black residue is __________. [zinc nitrate / copper nitrate]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Copper nitrate / Cu(NO3)2 / Copper(II) nitrate / Copper / Cu / cupric nitrate
key_points: Copper nitrate decomposes to give black CuO residue
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified copper nitrate. A few confused it with zinc nitrate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct answer from the brackets: During the electrolysis of copper sulphate solution, if ___________ is used as electrodes, the colour of the electrolyte does not fade. [copper / platinum]
key_points: Copper electrodes maintain concentration of CuSO4 solution
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates correctly identified copper.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct answer from the brackets: The process of heating the concentrated ore in a limited supply or absence of air is __________ [roasting / calcination]
key_points: Calcination involves heating in limited/absence of air
common_errors: Choosing roasting — roasting involves excess air
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates confused roasting with calcination.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: The group obtained by removing one hydrogen atom from the parent alkane.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly identified alkyl. Some confused it with alkyne. Some gave examples instead of term.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: Two metal plates or wires through which the current enters and leaves the electrolytic cell.
common_errors: Writing only cathode or only anode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most wrote cathode and anode. Some simply wrote electrodes.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: The amount of substance which contains the same number of units as the number of atoms in carbon-12.
common_errors: Writing relative molecular mass instead of mole
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority failed to write 'mole'. Most wrote relative molecular mass and lost marks.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: The tendency of an atom to pull a shared pair of electrons towards itself in a compound.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. Some confused with electron affinity.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: The formula which represents the simplest ratio between the atoms of elements present in a compound.
common_errors: Writing molecular formula instead of empirical formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many incorrectly answered molecular formula. Confusion between empirical and molecular formula.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name of the organic compound represented by the structural formula: H-C(H)(H)-C(Cl)(H)-C(Cl)(H)-C(H)(H)-C(H)(H)-H (2,3-dichloropentane structure)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most wrote '2 chloro, 3 chloropentane' instead of using 'di' prefix. Some wrote pentene instead of pentane.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name of the organic compound represented by the structural formula: H-C(H)(H)-C(H)(H)-C(=O)-OH (propanoic acid structure)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most confused propanoic acid with propanol or propanal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural diagram for the following organic compound: 3-methyl pentane
marking_schemes.scheme_text: H3C-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3 or full structural formula showing CH3 branch at C3
key_points: Correct number of hydrogen atoms satisfying tetravalency
accepted_alternatives: Full structural formula with all H atoms shown
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many drew correctly. A few misplaced the methyl group or gave wrong hydrogen count.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural diagram for the following organic compound: propyne
key_points: Triple bond between C2 and C3
accepted_alternatives: Full structural formula showing triple bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some drew correctly. Several failed to show carbon's tetravalency.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural diagram for the following organic compound: methanal
key_points: Double bond between C and O
accepted_alternatives: Full structural formula showing C=O double bond
common_errors: Failing to show double bond for oxygen
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many failed to depict the double bond for oxygen in methanal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Rewrite the following statement by adding the correct word: Given Statement: Sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concentrated Sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Concentrated Sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent.
common_errors: Writing only the word 'concentrated' without the full sentence
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many wrote only 'concentrated' without the full sentence and lost marks.

marking_schemes.question_text: Rewrite the following statement by adding the correct word: Given Statement: Ammonia reacts with chlorine to give ammonium chloride and nitrogen.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Excess ammonia reacts with chlorine to give ammonium chloride and nitrogen.
key_points: Word 'Excess' (referring to excess ammonia) must be added
marking_schemes.model_answer: Excess ammonia reacts with chlorine to give ammonium chloride and nitrogen.
common_errors: Confusing excess ammonia with excess chlorine reactions
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many wrote 'aqueous' instead of 'excess'. Confusion between two reactions of ammonia with chlorine.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify only the anion present in the following compound: The compound on heating produces a colourless, odourless gas which turns lime water milky and has no effect on acidified potassium dichromate solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Carbonate / Bicarbonate / hydrogen carbonate / CO3²⁻ / HCO3⁻
key_points: No effect on acidified K2Cr2O7 confirms it is not SO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many failed to identify the correct anion. Some provided wrong formula or wrong valency.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify only the anion present in the following compound: The solution of the compound which on treating with concentrated sulphuric acid and freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution produces a brown ring.
key_points: Brown ring test indicates nitrate ion
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most failed to identify nitrate as the anion. Some used wrong valency or wrong symbol.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mohan has three solutions P, Q and R having a pH of 13, 5 and 2 respectively. Which of the above solutions P, Q or R will react with Magnesium to liberate hydrogen gas?
key_points: Acidic solutions (pH < 7) react with Mg to give H2
Both R (pH 2) and Q (pH 5) are acidic
marking_schemes.model_answer: R (pH 2) and Q (pH 5) — both acidic solutions react with magnesium to liberate hydrogen gas.
common_errors: Choosing only one of R or Q
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some incorrectly identified only one option. Most correctly identified R and Q.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mohan has three solutions P, Q and R having a pH of 13, 5 and 2 respectively. Which of the above solutions P, Q or R will liberate ammonia gas when it reacts with ammonium chloride?
key_points: Alkaline solution (pH 13) reacts with NH4Cl to give NH3
marking_schemes.model_answer: P (pH 13) — alkaline solution liberates ammonia with ammonium chloride.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly answered P. A few incorrectly chose R.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mohan has three solutions P, Q and R having a pH of 13, 5 and 2 respectively. Which of the above solutions P, Q or R will contain molecules as well as ions?
key_points: Weak acid (pH 5) partially ionises — contains both molecules and ions
marking_schemes.model_answer: Q (pH 5) — a weak acid partially ionises, so it contains both molecules and ions.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered incorrectly. Confusion about particles present based on metal/nonmetal nature.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The following table is related to an Industrial process of an acid.
Name of the process | Reactant | Catalyst | Final product
(a) | SO2 + O2 | (b) | (c)
Identify (a), (b) and (c).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Contact process / oxidation / catalytic oxidation; (b) Vanadium Pentoxide / V2O5 / Platinum / Pt; (c) Sulphuric acid / H2SO4 / SO3 / sulphur trioxide
marking_schemes.model_answer: (a) Contact process; (b) V2O5 (Vanadium Pentoxide); (c) H2SO4 (Sulphuric acid)
common_errors: Confusing Contact Process with Ostwald Process or Bayer's Process
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some confused Contact Process with Ostwald or Bayer's process. Many correctly identified catalyst and product.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define the following term: Molar volume
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Molar Volume — Volume occupied by 1 gm molecular weight of a gas / or one mole of a gas at S.T.P.
key_points: Volume occupied by one mole of a gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Molar volume is the volume occupied by one gram molecular weight (one mole) of a gas at S.T.P.
accepted_alternatives: Volume occupied by 1 gram molecular weight of a gas at STP
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many unclear with concept. Several did not include STP. Some confused with RMM.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define the following term: Normal salt
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Normal Salt: The salts formed by complete/total replacement of the hydrogen of an acid molecule by a basic/base radical / metallic / ammonium ion. / Salt formed by complete neutralization of an acid by a base.
key_points: Complete neutralization of acid by base
marking_schemes.model_answer: A normal salt is formed by the complete replacement of all replaceable hydrogen ions of an acid by a metallic or ammonium ion.
accepted_alternatives: Salt formed by complete neutralization of an acid by a base
common_errors: Saying 'acid reacts with base to form salt and water' without mentioning complete replacement
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many missed key phrases like 'complete replacement of replaceable hydrogen ion'. Failed to specify 'metallic/ammonium ion'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot structure of: Methane molecule [Atomic number: C = 6, H = 1]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electron dot structure of CH4 showing 4 H atoms bonded to C with shared electron pairs using dots and crosses.
key_points: 4 C-H single bonds shown with electron pairs
Different notations for different atoms (dots vs crosses)
marking_schemes.model_answer: H atoms shown with crosses (×) and C with dots (•): each C-H bond shown as shared pair; C at centre with 4 H atoms around it.
accepted_alternatives: Any correct electron dot structure showing 4 shared pairs
common_errors: Using same notation for both atoms
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most drew correctly. Some used same notation for both elements or placed bonds between dots.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot structure of: Nitrogen molecule [Atomic number: N = 7]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: :N:::N: or •N≡N• showing triple bond with lone pairs on each N
key_points: Triple bond between two N atoms
One lone pair on each N atom
Different notations for the two atoms
marking_schemes.model_answer: :N≡N: (lone pair on each N, triple bond between them)
common_errors: Forgetting lone pairs on nitrogen atoms
Only showing triple bond without lone pairs
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly but some forgot to include lone pairs on N atoms not involved in bonding.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete and balance the following equation: Al2O3 + NaOH →
common_errors: Writing aluminium hydroxide and sodium oxide as products
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many wrote aluminium hydroxide and sodium oxide as incorrect products. Confusion with sodium aluminate formula.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete and balance the following equation (with CaO and heat conditions): C2H5COONa + NaOH →
marking_schemes.scheme_text: C2H5COONa + NaOH → C2H6 + Na2CO3 (with CaO, heat)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly. A few made errors in balancing or overbalanced.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete and balance the following equation: C2H4Br2 + alcoholic KOH →
common_errors: Writing H2 instead of H2O as product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most could not answer correctly. Many wrote C2H6, failed to balance, or wrote hydrogen instead of water.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the organic compound from the list given below to answer the following question: Ethene, Ethanoic acid, Ethanol, Methanal. The compound which does not have a double bond in its structure.
key_points: No double bond in ethanol structure
common_errors: Choosing ethene due to presence of double bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly. Some chose ethene or ethanoic acid without reading carefully.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the organic compound from the list given below to answer the following question: Ethene, Ethanoic acid, Ethanol, Methanal. The compound which in its pure form turns into an ice like solid on cooling.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ethanoic acid / acetic acid / glacial acetic acid / CH3COOH
key_points: Ethanoic acid freezes to a solid (glacial acetic acid) on cooling
common_errors: Choosing other options from the list
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly chose ethanoic acid. Some were confused and selected other options.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the organic compound from the list given below to answer the following question: Ethene, Ethanoic acid, Ethanol, Methanal. The compound which is used for artificial ripening of fruits.
key_points: Ethene is used for artificial ripening of fruits
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified ethene. A few mistakenly chose ethanol.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the main metal used in making of the alloy: Duralumin
key_points: Aluminium is the main metal in Duralumin
common_errors: Listing additional components without emphasising aluminium as primary metal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified Aluminium. Some listed additional components without highlighting the main metal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the main metal used in making of the alloy: Stainless steel
key_points: Iron is the main metal in stainless steel
common_errors: Listing all components without highlighting iron as primary metal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified iron. Some listed full composition without highlighting the main metal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Sulphuric acid and Nitric acid using barium chloride solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sulphuric acid forms a ppt / insoluble substance or Barium sulphate when treated with BaCl2 but HNO3 does not form any ppt. / or forms soluble substance / no such observations / no visible change.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sulphuric acid forms a white precipitate of Barium Sulphate (BaSO4) when treated with BaCl2 solution, whereas Nitric acid does not form any precipitate with BaCl2.
accepted_alternatives: H2SO4 gives white ppt with BaCl2; HNO3 gives no visible change
common_errors: Noting a brown precipitate with nitric acid
Failing to note absence of precipitate with nitric acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many could not differentiate. Some noted incorrect brown precipitate with nitric acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Unsaturated and Saturated hydrocarbons based on type of bond present.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a double or triple bond whereas a saturated hydrocarbon has only single bonds.
key_points: Unsaturated: double or triple bond (= or ≡)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain double or triple bonds (C=C or C≡C), whereas saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds (C-C).
accepted_alternatives: Correct structural examples showing bond differences
common_errors: Giving examples instead of bond types
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most accurately distinguished bond types. A few confused the concepts.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid as given below: CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. What is the mass of 5 moles of calcium carbonate? (Relative molecular mass of calcium carbonate is 100)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most calculated 500 g correctly. Some lost marks for writing answer directly without working.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid as given below: CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. How many moles of HCl will react with 5 moles of calcium carbonate?
key_points: From equation: 1 mole CaCO3 reacts with 2 moles HCl
5 moles CaCO3 reacts with 10 moles HCl
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most determined 10 moles correctly. A few made calculation errors.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid as given below: CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. What is the volume of carbon dioxide liberated at S.T.P. at the same time?
marking_schemes.model_answer: Volume of CO2 = 5 × 22.4 = 112 L at STP
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many calculated correctly. Many others just wrote 22.4 L without proper calculation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the gas evolved in the following reaction: Methane undergoes complete combustion.
key_points: Complete combustion of methane produces CO2 and H2O
common_errors: Writing carbonate CO3²⁻ instead of CO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly. A few identified it as carbonate ion instead of CO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the gas evolved in the following reaction: Copper carbonate is heated.
key_points: Thermal decomposition of CuCO3 gives CO2 and CuO
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly. A few wrote carbon monoxide instead.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the gas evolved in the following reaction: MnO2 reacts with concentrated HCl.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cl2 / Chlorine / Cl / greenish yellow gas
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many wrote Chlorine correctly but lost marks for writing formula as Cl instead of Cl2.

marking_schemes.question_text: X - HCl ⇋ H⁺ + Cl⁻ (in solution state); Y - PbBr2 ⇋ Pb²⁺ + 2Br⁻ (in molten state). From the above reactions X or Y, identify the reaction which exhibits: electrolytic dissociation
key_points: Ionic compound PbBr2 in molten state undergoes electrolytic dissociation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most identified Y correctly. A few confused with ionization.

marking_schemes.question_text: X - HCl ⇋ H⁺ + Cl⁻ (in solution state); Y - PbBr2 ⇋ Pb²⁺ + 2Br⁻ (in molten state). From the above reactions X or Y, identify the reaction which exhibits: ionization
key_points: Covalent compound HCl ionises in solution state
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority failed to recognize X as ionization. Many confused the two processes.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give reason for the following: Inert gases do not form ions.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Because their outermost shell is complete / they have stable electronic configuration / they do not lose or donate electrons / octet or duplet state.
key_points: Do not lose or gain electrons
marking_schemes.model_answer: Inert gases do not form ions because their outermost shell is completely filled (octet/duplet), giving them a stable electronic configuration and no tendency to lose or gain electrons.
accepted_alternatives: Stable electronic configuration / complete outermost shell
common_errors: Writing 'because they are inert' without reasoning
Writing 'cannot participate in chemical reactions' without mentioning electronic configuration
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly stated stable electronic configuration. Some wrote vague answers without keywords.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Give reason for the following: Covalent compounds have a low melting and boiling point.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Because they have a weak force of attraction / Van der Waal's force of attraction between the molecules/particles.
key_points: Weak Van der Waals forces between molecules
marking_schemes.model_answer: Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points because they have weak Van der Waals forces of attraction between their molecules.
common_errors: Writing 'weak electrostatic forces' instead of Van der Waals
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most failed to use keywords 'Van der Waals forces between the molecules'. Some wrote weak electrostatic forces.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange the following in decreasing order of atomic size: Carbon, Fluorine, Beryllium
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Beryllium, Carbon, Fluorine / Be, C, F / Be > C > F
key_points: Atomic size decreases across a period left to right
common_errors: Reversing the order: F, C, Be
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many incorrectly arranged or confused greater/lesser symbols. Some wrote opposite sequence.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange the following in increasing order of number of replaceable H atoms per molecule: Sulphuric acid, Phosphoric acid, Acetic acid
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Acetic acid < Sulphuric acid < Phosphoric acid
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Acetic acid, Sulphuric acid, Phosphoric acid
marking_schemes.model_answer: Acetic acid (1) < Sulphuric acid (2) < Phosphoric acid (3)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many failed to arrange correctly. Confusion about basicity of each acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange the following in increasing order of ionization potential: Potassium, Lithium, Sodium
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Potassium, Sodium, Lithium / K < Na < Li / K, Na, Li
key_points: Li > Na > K in ionization potential
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correct but many wrote reverse order. A few confused with trend.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify: An element in period 1 which can be placed in both group 1 and group 17 of the Periodic Table.
key_points: Hydrogen can be placed in Group 1 (1 valence electron) and Group 17 (needs 1 electron to complete shell)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly identified hydrogen. A few wrote lithium.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify: The element having electronic configuration 2, 8, 6.
common_errors: Confusing atomic number with electronic configuration
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly. A few confused due to atomic number and electronic configuration.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify: The most electronegative element of period 3.
key_points: Chlorine is the most electronegative element in Period 3 (excluding noble gas Argon)
common_errors: Writing Fluorine or Bromine (they are in different periods)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many confused and wrote fluorine or bromine. Some confused chlorine with its electronegativity.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Rita was given an unknown salt for identification. To the first part of the salt solution, she added a few drops of ammonium hydroxide and obtained a reddish-brown precipitate. Name the cation present in the salt.
key_points: Reddish-brown precipitate with NH4OH indicates Fe³⁺
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly identified but some wrote Fe²⁺ or omitted the charge. Some listed two cations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Rita was given an unknown salt for identification. To the second part of the salt solution, she added a few drops of silver nitrate solution and obtained a white precipitate. Name the anion present in the salt.
key_points: White precipitate with AgNO3 indicates Cl⁻ (AgCl) or SO4²⁻
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few correctly identified the anion. Many listed both cation and anion or only identified the cation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct answer from the bracket: Carbon tetrachloride is a __________ [polar / non-polar] covalent molecule.
key_points: CCl4 is a non-polar covalent molecule due to symmetrical structure
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified non-polar. A few confused with polar.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct answer from the bracket: During electrolysis of acidulated water, the gas liberated at the anode is ___________ [oxygen / hydrogen].
key_points: Oxygen is liberated at the anode during electrolysis of acidulated water
common_errors: Choosing hydrogen (hydrogen is liberated at cathode, not anode)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly answered oxygen. Some confused anode and cathode products.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ammonia burns in oxygen as shown below: 4NH3 + 3O2 → 2N2 + 6H2O. If 240 cc of ammonia is burnt in 300 cc of oxygen, find out the composition of the resultant gaseous mixture at room temperature.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: O2 used = (3/4) x 240 = 180 cc; Excess O2 = 300 – 180 = 120 cc; N2 produced = (2/4) x 240 = 120 cc; Resultant mixture contains 120 cc of O2 and 120 cc of N2
key_points: Water is liquid at room temperature so not included in gaseous mixture
Final gaseous mixture: 120 cc O2 + 120 cc N2
marking_schemes.model_answer: O2 consumed = (3/4) × 240 = 180 cc. Excess O2 = 300 - 180 = 120 cc. N2 produced = (2/4) × 240 = 120 cc. Since water is liquid at room temperature, resultant gaseous mixture = 120 cc O2 + 120 cc N2.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many calculated O2 used and unused but failed to calculate N2 formed. Some only noted N2 as 120 cc ignoring excess O2.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following table shows the electronic configuration of atoms A(2,8,8,2), B(2,6), C(2,8,7), D(2,4). Write the formula of the compound formed between A and B.
key_points: A has 2 valence electrons (Group 2), B has 6 valence electrons (Group 16)
A²⁺ combines with B²⁻ in 1:1 ratio giving AB
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly answered AB. A few misunderstood and wrote A2B2.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following table shows the electronic configuration of atoms A(2,8,8,2), B(2,6), C(2,8,7), D(2,4). Write the formula of the compound formed between D and C.
key_points: D has 4 valence electrons, C has 7 valence electrons (needs 1 more)
D bonds with 4 C atoms giving DC4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly with DC4. A few wrote incorrect formulas.

marking_schemes.question_text: The following table shows the electronic configuration of atoms A(2,8,8,2), B(2,6), C(2,8,7), D(2,4). Which of the above elements will exhibit catenation?
key_points: Carbon exhibits catenation — ability to bond with itself
common_errors: Selecting multiple elements from the table
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly answered D. Some selected multiple options.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer from the list given below: zinc blende, C2H2, calamine, CH, haematite. The ore which can be concentrated by magnetic separation.
key_points: Haematite (Fe2O3) is a magnetic ore concentrated by magnetic separation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified haematite. A few chose zinc blende.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer from the list given below: zinc blende, C2H2, calamine, CH, haematite. Empirical formula of Ethyne.
key_points: Ethyne (C2H2): ratio C:H = 1:1, empirical formula = CH
common_errors: Writing C2H2 (molecular formula) instead of CH (empirical formula)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many incorrectly wrote C2H2 instead of CH. Many correctly identified CH.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give balanced equation for the following reaction: Copper reacts with concentrated Nitric acid.
common_errors: Writing dilute nitric acid reaction (gives NO not NO2)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many wrote products for dilute HNO3 reaction. Many could not balance correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give balanced equation for the following reaction: Aluminium nitride is treated with warm water.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several wrote aluminium oxide instead of aluminium hydroxide. Some had wrong formula for AlN.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the salts underlined in Column A with the most suitable method of preparation given in Column B: ZnCl2 from Zn
key_points: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2 is a displacement reaction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many chose combination or neutralization incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the salts underlined in Column A with the most suitable method of preparation given in Column B: KNO3 from KOH
key_points: KOH + HNO3 → KNO3 + H2O is neutralization
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified neutralization.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the salts underlined in Column A with the most suitable method of preparation given in Column B: CaCO3 from CaCl2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few found this difficult. Most correctly identified precipitation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory by the action of concentrated sulphuric acid on sodium chloride. Give balanced chemical equation for the above reaction.
common_errors: Using high temperature conditions giving Na2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many incorrectly used higher temperature conditions. Some provided wrong products.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory by the action of concentrated sulphuric acid on sodium chloride. State the method of collection of the gas formed above.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Upward displacement of air / downward delivery of gas
key_points: HCl is denser than air, collected by upward displacement of air (downward delivery of gas)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Upward displacement of air (downward delivery of gas)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many provided incorrect answers. Confusion between upward/downward displacement and delivery.

marking_schemes.question_text: Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory by the action of concentrated sulphuric acid on sodium chloride. What is the property of sulphuric acid that makes it a suitable reagent for the reaction?
key_points: H2SO4 is non-volatile/least volatile — it displaces volatile HCl
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sulphuric acid is a non-volatile (least volatile) acid, which allows it to displace the more volatile HCl gas.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified non-volatile property. A few described it as dehydrating agent or dibasic acid.
